A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CGNN research. All 15 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2, including appendices and post-reference proofs, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification, efficiency, and component experiments, plus link-prediction and sensitivity results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 reports original node-classification results on eight datasets, efficiency and component experiments, and a new analysis of commute-time changes after rewiring.

M1.justification: The DiLap formulation, feature-similarity rewiring, randomized-SVD computation, and commute-weighted incoming/outgoing aggregation are retained. Algorithm 1 is unchanged and moves from Appendix B to Section 5.4. The new rewiring experiment evaluates the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds node classification on Snap-Patents, Roman-Empire, and Arxiv-Year while retaining the original five datasets, substantially extending coverage, including much larger graphs. It removes both edge-direction and edge-existence prediction on Citeseer and CoraML from v1 Appendix D.1.

E2.justification: v2 Table 2 retains all 12 original node-classification baselines and adds DUPLEX, including comparisons on the original five datasets. This is a limited comparator addition; the prose still says 12 baselines despite the table containing 13.

E3.justification: The retained node-classification split rules and accuracy metric are unchanged. However, v2 introduces largest-connected-component selection, removal of absorbing nodes, and a relative normalized-commute-time difference measure for its rewiring study. It also removes the link-prediction protocol using 15% test and 5% validation edges and the depth/width sweep protocol alongside those experiments, substantially changing the reported evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct test of whether rewiring preserves commute times on CoraML, Chameleon, and Roman-Empire (Section 6.5, Table 5). It removes the depth and hidden-width sensitivity analysis on Squirrel and CoraML (v1 Appendix D.2, Figure 5). The existing PPR, directed-versus-undirected, and label-proximity analyses remain, but the supplementary questions investigated change substantially.

E5.justification: Both main classification tables report accuracy with standard deviation over 10 runs, and both versions specify 10 public splits for Squirrel and Chameleon. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed repetition counts are reported. Additional result entries and changed standard-deviation values do not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds DUPLEX results and three dataset columns, with CGNN leading six of eight datasets versus four of five in v1; DirGNN leads the added Snap-Patents comparison, 73.95 versus CGNN's 72.33. Reported CGNN scores change from 77.20±2.42 to 77.61±1.87 on Squirrel and 77.02±0.67 to 77.06±0.67 on CoraML. Citeseer accuracies in the PPR comparison change from 80.27/78.59 to 70.27/68.59 for CGNN/CGNNppr. v2 also adds three rewiring-change results and removes the link-prediction and sensitivity results.

T1.justification: The core assumptions, DiLap equations, commute-time theorems, and proofs are retained. The complexity analysis changes from O(q|E|) in v1 Appendix B to O((Ld^2+q)|E|) in v2 Section 5.4, explicitly accounting for message-passing depth and feature dimension. Section 6.5 also defines the relative commute-time-change quantity used in the new analysis.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain DiLap, efficient commute-time computation, and commute-weighted directed message passing to capture asymmetric mutual relationships. The added abstract sentence about superior performance and the expanded conclusion restate claims already made in v1's introduction and conclusion; the additional datasets broaden their supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 Section 6.3 introduces an explicit applicability argument: commute weighting may be unnecessary or harmful in chronological citation networks without mutual paths, while being particularly useful in networks with mutual relationships. This materially qualifies the earlier broad effectiveness discussion. v1's interpretation that heterophilic graphs benefit from deeper aggregation, based on its sensitivity analysis, is removed.

D1.justification: v1 Appendix C.3 and Table 5 disclose validation-based hyperparameter selection, learning-rate and weight-decay search ranges, and dataset-specific depths and hidden dimensions. These disclosures are absent from v2, substantially reducing reproducibility information. Hardware, split descriptions, and pseudocode are retained through relocation; rank q=5 remains mentioned, but only as a typical choice.

R1.justification: v2 expands Section 2.2 with Holonets, magnetic framelet networks, Sigmanet, directed-acyclic-graph transformers, and DUPLEX, and adds a GNN survey citation in the complexity discussion. These broaden the literature context without substantially changing CGNN's positioning relative to existing Laplacians and DirGNN.

P1.justification: The document undergoes substantial structural reorganization: notation and DirGNN receive a separate Preliminary section, pseudocode and experimental settings move from appendices into the main narrative, and the proof appendix becomes Section 8. The conclusion is rewritten, and citation style and author/header text change, although much of the technical prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a wider page layout with running date headers and redistributes figures, tables, and Algorithm 1. The dataset and classification tables expand, a rewiring-results table is added, and the hyperparameter table, link-prediction table, and sensitivity heatmaps disappear. The directed-structure display is retained and relabeled from Figure 4 to Table 6; the main explanatory diagrams and efficiency plots remain.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful evidence from larger graphs, DUPLEX comparisons, and a direct rewiring study, while making the complexity expression more informative and correcting the inconsistent Citeseer comparison entries. However, it removes link-prediction and sensitivity evidence and, more seriously, the detailed hyperparameter documentation needed for reproduction. These material gains in empirical coverage and losses in reproducibility and complementary validation do not support a reliably assessable net quality direction.
